sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Boxtel, a small town in Noord-Brabant with an important railway station, charges modestly for street parking and wants cars at the edge of the centre. The council adopted the parking tax ordinance for 2026 on 4 November 2025: paid street parking costs 0.21 euro per 12 minutes in the first and second hour, about 1.05 euros an hour, and 0.41 euro per 12 minutes after that, unchanged from 2024 and 2025 [0]. Permits cost 32.25 euros a quarter, 129 euros a year, for a plate-bound permit for the part of the paid area where the holder lives, up to 119.50 euros a quarter, 478 euros a year, for a non-plate-bound permit for the whole area [1]. A parking-disc zone of two hours, set in 2017, covers Breukelen-Zuid and the centre west of the Dommel, including Stationsplein, and was valid Monday to Thursday from 9.00 to 18.00, Friday until 21.00 and Saturday until 17.30; later changes were not checked, and the municipal site was offline when we looked [13]. In March 2025 the Stationsstraat became a pedestrian zone with loading from 7.00 to 13.00 [14]. The Programma Duurzame Mobiliteit of January 2025 aims for a car-light centre with long-stay parking at its edges, says the municipality does not size parking for peak days or events, and says a blue zone around the station keeps out long-stay train travellers [6]. New parking norms published on 23 January 2026 apply the lowest end of the national range to housing in a new area within about ten minutes' walk of the station, and let developers in the centre pay 10,000 euros per missing space into a municipal fund, if a survey shows spare public capacity [3][4].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The Omgevingsvisie, adopted on 4 February 2025, says the station is to be developed into a mobility hub, with car access and parking remaining important but moved more towards the edges, and announces area programmes for the town and the station area [5]. The province names Boxtel station a regional node, and the programme mentions the P+R on the west side of the station in connection with links from the villages [7]. By a decision signed on 21 September 2026 the municipality designated 48 parking spaces for charging only in Boxtel and Liempde, after nine locations were dropped following views on the draft; the points come from a contract that the provinces of Noord-Brabant and Limburg signed with Vattenfall [8].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The 2017 parking vision records an agreement with NS of 2013 to introduce permit parking around the NS car park on the centre side of the station, in return for NS providing bicycle storage, and an agreement of December 2016 that regulating the Parallelweg Noord car park would be an effective way to meet it, so that train travellers use the NS facility on the west side [12]. Q-Park's page for P+R Van Salmstraat shows 193 spaces, open round the clock, with a discount for rail travellers; its tariff did not load [15]. The exemptions in the disc zone are handled by P1 On Street B.V. under a service agreement of 2017 [11]. The only measurement of parking pressure we found is a survey of October 2016, which found no overall shortage in the centre but a distribution problem, with some locations above the accepted pressure at busy times; it is old [10].

Our data cover the P+R Van Salmstraat, with 193 spaces, for about 61 days since 22 August 2026. Occupancy averaged about 33% on weekdays and 29% at weekends, with a peak of 70% around midday on a Thursday. The centre's other parking is not in our data.
